summary: deploy.sh: pass -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 to psql so silent migration errors halt the deploy
description:
deploy.sh's migration loop runs psql with -1 (single transaction) but no ON_ERROR_STOP. SQL errors abort the transaction and emit ERROR lines, but psql still exits 0 — so deploy.sh's set -e doesn't catch the failure and the deploy continues. The just-shipped PR #27 surfaced this when CREATE INDEX statements hit 'must be owner' errors and the deploy moved on as if migrations had applied (they hadn't).

Fix: add -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 to the psql invocation. One-line change:

  -  sudo -u guru /usr/bin/psql -d guru -1 < "$f"
  +  sudo -u guru /usr/bin/psql -d guru -1 -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 < "$f"

Sudoers stanza must extend to permit the new arg form:

  -  deploy ALL=(guru) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/psql -d guru -1
  +  deploy ALL=(guru) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/psql -d guru -1 -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1

Existing VPSes need the one-time visudo edit.

Done when:
- deploy.sh psql call includes -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1
- vps-bootstrap.sh sudoers stanza updated
- README documents the one-time hand-patch on existing VPSes
- Test asserts the flag is present in deploy.sh and the sudoers stanza

resolution.note: psql now exits non-zero on first SQL error; deploy halts visibly. Sudoers stanza extended to permit the new arg form; existing VPS needs one-line visudo edit.
